lesson: Zero RFIs on a project is a red flag that nobody asked the right questions, not a win to brag about.
detail: Did you actually have line of sight to your risk profile before field execution? RFI quality, not count, is the signal.
role: Senior Director of VDC, McCarthy Building Companies

lesson: One retiring veteran takes five new hires to replace. The real labor shortage is knowledge leaving, not bodies missing.
detail: Roughly 400,000 workers retire annually against about 100,000 apprentice completions. The productivity gap is what kills a crew, not the headcount gap.

lesson: The real AI risk is not security. It is someone shipping the first draft as the final draft.
detail: Corporate AI policies obsess over data leakage while the actual damage comes from people treating the tool as an easy button and skipping review.

lesson: You cannot fix a bad buy. Scope missed at buyout comes straight out of margin with no way to recover it.
detail: Buyout is the highest-stakes irreversible moment in construction.

lesson: Finishing on schedule and budget only buys you the right to bid the next one. The career gets built in moments not in the contract.
detail: The relationships that carry a PM or super come from small, unscripted moments with the client.

lesson: The GC that can bid its CM fee at zero wins, because the margin lives in supply, insurance, and equipment.
detail: Turner's SourceBlue, insurance brokerage, and equipment rentals make the fee a loss leader. A GC stuck doing a little of everything will fail.

lesson: Do not bring in another point solution unless it eliminates two or three existing ones. Otherwise you just added a login.
detail: The industry is littered with purpose-built apps for the 150 processes on a project, and every extra one adds noise and data bottlenecks.

lesson: When you try to automate a process you discover how much unpriced judgment the 'not that bright' guy was adding.
detail: Pulling a human out of a process trades quality for new risk nobody budgeted. The embedded intelligence only shows up once it is gone.

lesson: Field tech does not save you months on the schedule. It gives you your time back and real data when a dispute lands.
detail: The honest ROI is the superintendent's personal time plus defensible records in a conflict. Expecting schedule compression sets up disappointment.

lesson: Put model due, signed off, shop drawings in, and approved for install in the field schedule and track them like a bottom-out date.
detail: VDC milestones that live outside the super's schedule slip silently and eat field float.

lesson: The schedule is the plan. Perfect RFIs and submittals cannot save a job where nobody trusts or is aligned to it.
detail: A schedule the team does not believe in is worse than none. Fix plan trust before buying any other PM tool.

lesson: If your tool is harder than the hand signature it replaces, crews revert, and everybody in their network hears about it.
detail: Weeks of training plus an unkept promise sends users back to the old way, and the lost trust is nearly impossible to recover in a relationship-driven industry.

lesson: Prefab is a manufacturing business, not construction in a warehouse, and running it with a construction mindset is how you get burned.
detail: Manufacturing processes, work instructions, and controlled environments demand a paradigm shift from field habits. He admits he did not appreciate the difference at first.

lesson: It is not the guy in the trailer that builds the job. Make young PMs lay block and walk steel so they respect the craft.
detail: The Building Skills program forced young project managers to do trade work to understand what makes a 20-year plasterer's work look effortless.
